source_text: Tu tamen argumentando et testimonia Scripturarum usurpando de hac illum concupiscentia, quam legem peccati vocas, et omnes sanctos tam pollutos quam conquestos fuisse confirmas.
pass_a_gloss: You nevertheless by arguing and usurping the testimonies of the Scriptures confirm that of this desire, which you call the law of sin, both all the saints were as polluted as having complained.

lemmas.lexica: LS concupiscentia=eager desire; Blaise Christian usage often sexual desire vs nuptiae
LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS lex; Blaise lex Dei / sacred Law

pass_b_english: Yet by argument and by appropriating Scripture’s testimonies, you maintain that this desire, which you call the law of sin, both polluted him and all the saints and drew their complaints (Romans 7:23).

choices.why: Julian distinguishes nuptiae from concupiscentia; do not flatten to 'lust' as a nature-sin substance.
Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
